name: System Design: High-Level and Low-Level Design
certifications: No vendor certification; assessed by design reviews and mock interviews
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate as a companion certification
tools: Java, Python or C# for low-level design

beginner.summary: For developers preparing for design interviews or moving into design work. Covers a method for design problems, requirements and estimates, client-server basics and APIs, SQL and NoSQL choices, scaling out with load balancers, caching, CDNs, replication, partitioning, queues, consistency and CAP, classic problems such as a URL shortener, rate limiter and notification system, object-oriented principles and SOLID, design patterns, low-level design problems, storage choices and how to communicate a design.
prerequisites: Has built at least one web application or API
Understands databases at a basic level
outcomes: Approach design problems with a repeatable method
Use the building blocks of scalable systems
Solve classic high-level and low-level design problems

days.topic: System Design Overview and How to Approach Problems
subtopics: What system design covers: high-level and low-level design
Where system design is used at work and in interviews
A step-by-step method for any design problem
days.lab_task: Apply the design method to a simple file sharing service: ask clarifying questions, list requirements, draw a first diagram, deep-dive into storage and record the trade-offs.
checks: At least eight useful questions asked before designing
Clients, services and data stores shown with flows
Two choices explained with pros and cons

subtopics: Availability, latency, durability and consistency targets
Powers of two and latency numbers
Estimating storage, bandwidth and requests per second
days.lab_task: Write requirements for a social media app and estimate daily active users, requests per second, storage for five years and bandwidth, then explain how the numbers shape the design.
checks: Requests per second and storage estimated with steps shown
Two design choices justified by the numbers

subtopics: Clients, servers and the request lifecycle
HTTP methods, status codes and headers
days.lab_task: Trace a request from a browser to a server through DNS, load balancer and application, design REST endpoints for a to-do service and pick a protocol for live updates.
checks: Each hop from browser to database explained
Endpoints follow REST conventions with status codes

subtopics: Choosing a database from access patterns
days.lab_task: For five sample products, list access patterns and choose a database type for each, then model one in SQL and one in a document store.
checks: Each choice justified by access patterns
Relational schema supports the main queries

days.topic: Scaling Out: Vertical Scaling, Horizontal Scaling and Load Balancers
days.lab_task: Scale a small web app from one to three servers behind NGINX, make it stateless, compare round robin and least connections under load and remove a single point of failure.
days.deliverable: Scaled setup with load test results
checks: Sessions survive when a server is removed
Remove a single point of failure
Design survives losing any one node

subtopics: Where to cache: client, CDN, server and database
days.lab_task: Add cache-aside caching with Redis to a product service, choose expiry and invalidation rules, protect against a stampede and measure hit ratio and latency.
checks: Cached reads faster than database reads
Updates visible after the agreed delay
Only one rebuild for many concurrent misses

tools: A CDN such as CloudFront or Cloudflare
days.lab_task: Put a CDN in front of a static site and an API, cache assets with versioned names, set cache headers for API responses and measure latency from two regions.
checks: New release served without manual invalidation
Edge latency lower than origin latency

days.lab_task: Set up a PostgreSQL primary and replica, route reads to the replica, show replication lag, handle read-after-write for a user's own data and practise a failover.
Choose shard keys for a messaging app and a store, simulate data distribution for each, find a hot spot and design rebalancing.
checks: Data spread evenly with the chosen key
Hot spot found and a fix proposed

days.lab_task: Move image processing in a photo app to a queue, design idempotent workers, add a dead letter queue and show how the queue absorbs a traffic spike.
checks: Queue grows and drains while the API stays fast
Failing messages moved aside after retries

days.topic: Consistency, Availability and the CAP Theorem
subtopics: Consistency models: strong, eventual and causal
days.lab_task: Choose a consistency model for ten features of a banking and a social app, explain each with CAP and PACELC, and show a quorum setting that gives strong reads.
checks: Each feature has a model and reason
Read and write quorum settings give strong reads

days.lab_task: Design a URL shortener for 100 million links a month, compare code generation strategies, choose storage, cache hot links and add click analytics without slowing redirects.
checks: Hashing, counters and random codes compared
Click counting does not slow redirects

subtopics: Where to put a rate limiter
Limits per user, IP and API key
Responses and headers for limited requests
days.lab_task: Design a distributed rate limiter, implement a sliding window limiter with Redis, test it under concurrent load and handle Redis being unavailable.
checks: Requests beyond the limit rejected with 429

days.lab_task: Design a notification system for 10 million users across email, SMS and push with preferences, retries, provider failover and delivery tracking.
checks: Each channel has its own queue and workers

days.topic: Low-Level Design: Object-Oriented Principles and SOLID
days.lab_task: Refactor a tangled billing module to follow SOLID, draw class and sequence diagrams before and after, and show how a new payment type is added without changing old code.
checks: Class and sequence diagrams match the code
New type added without editing existing classes

days.topic: Low-Level Design: Design Patterns in Practice
subtopics: Creational patterns: factory, builder and singleton
Structural patterns: adapter, decorator and facade
Behavioural patterns: strategy, observer and state
Choosing a pattern from the problem
days.lab_task: Solve six small problems with the right pattern each, explain why the pattern fits, write tests and remove one pattern that adds no value.
checks: Each problem solved with a fitting pattern
Unneeded pattern removed with simpler code

days.topic: Low-Level Design Problems: Parking Lot and Library System
subtopics: Explaining the design in an interview
days.lab_task: Design and code a parking lot system and a library management system with class diagrams, extension points, thread-safe allocation and tests, then present one in a mock interview.
days.deliverable: Two low-level designs with code and tests
checks: Concurrent parking requests never double-book a spot
Follow-up questions answered in a mock interview

days.topic: Storage Choices: Blob Storage, Files and Search Indexes
subtopics: Object storage for files and media
Metadata in databases and files in object storage
tools: Object storage such as Amazon S3 or MinIO
days.lab_task: Design storage for a video learning platform with object storage for videos, a relational store for metadata, a search index for courses and lifecycle rules for old content.
checks: Each data type mapped to a store with reasons
Course search served by the index
Monthly storage cost estimated with lifecycle rules

days.topic: Communicating a Design: Diagrams and Trade-offs
subtopics: Diagram levels with the C4 model
days.lab_task: Write a short design document with C4 diagrams for the notification system, present it in ten minutes, take questions and review a classmate's design.
checks: Context and container diagrams clear to a newcomer

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Designing a Photo Sharing Service
days.lab_task: Design a photo sharing service end to end with requirements, estimates, a high-level design with caching, CDN, replication and queues, a low-level design of the upload module in code, and present it.
checks: Capacity estimates support the design choices
Upload module code follows the low-level design
objectives: Combine the beginner topics in one design

intermediate.summary: For developers and senior engineers preparing for design rounds or design responsibilities. Covers classic large designs (news feed, chat, autocomplete, video streaming, ride sharing, key-value store, web crawler and payments), consistent hashing, distributed transactions, leader election and consensus, event-driven and streaming designs, API style choices, reliability and disaster recovery, observability, security, concurrency in low-level design, further low-level design problems and mock interviews.
prerequisites: Comfortable with caching, replication, sharding and queues
Writes object-oriented code in one language
outcomes: Design large real-world systems with sound trade-offs
Solve advanced low-level design problems with concurrency
Perform well in system design interviews

subtopics: Fan-out on write compared with fan-out on read
days.lab_task: Design a news feed for 200 million users, choose a hybrid fan-out for celebrities, design feed storage and caching, and explain how deletes and privacy changes propagate.
checks: Hybrid approach justified with load numbers
Feed reads served mostly from cache
Deleted posts removed from feeds within the target time

days.lab_task: Design a chat system with WebSocket gateways, ordered message storage, receipts, presence, offline delivery and large groups, and explain the scaling limits.
checks: Offline messages delivered with push notifications

days.lab_task: Design autocomplete with a sharded trie built from query logs, ranking, prefix caching and safe filtering, and implement a small trie with top-k suggestions.
checks: Trie returns the top five suggestions for a prefix
Design meets the latency target with caching

days.lab_task: Design a video platform with an upload and transcoding pipeline, adaptive streaming through a CDN, view counting and cost estimates for storage and bandwidth.
checks: Pipeline produces several renditions in parallel
View counts scale without hot rows

days.lab_task: Design ride matching with geospatial indexing for live driver locations, a trip state machine and surge pricing, and implement a small geohash-based nearby search.
days.deliverable: Ride-sharing design and nearby search code
checks: Nearby search returns drivers within the radius
State machine covers cancellations and failures

subtopics: Storage engines: LSM trees and B-trees
days.lab_task: Design a Dynamo-style key-value store with consistent hashing, replication, quorums, conflict resolution and failure detection, and implement a consistent hashing ring.
days.deliverable: Key-value store design and hashing ring code
checks: Only a small share of keys move
Settings meet the stated consistency target
Conflict example resolved with the chosen method

subtopics: Robots rules and rate limits per host
days.lab_task: Design a crawler for one billion pages a month with a prioritised frontier, politeness per host, duplicate detection and trap handling, and code a small polite crawler.
checks: Crawler waits between requests to one host
Fetch capacity estimated for the target

days.lab_task: Design a payment system with idempotent requests, a double-entry ledger, provider integration, reconciliation and safe retries, and code the ledger posting logic.
days.deliverable: Payment system design and ledger code
checks: Mismatches between ledger and provider found

subtopics: Why simple hashing breaks when nodes change
days.lab_task: Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes and rendezvous hashing, compare key movement and balance when nodes join and leave, and handle a hot key.
checks: Load spread measured with and without virtual nodes
Keys moved measured for both methods
Hot key spread with a proposed technique

days.topic: Distributed Transactions and Sagas in System Design
days.lab_task: Design a travel booking flow across flights, hotels and payments using two-phase commit and then a saga, compare failure handling and pick one with reasons.
checks: Compensation steps cover each failure point
Choice justified by availability and complexity

subtopics: Coordination services such as ZooKeeper and etcd
Where consensus appears in real systems
days.lab_task: Use etcd for leader election between three workers, show split brain without fencing, fix it with fencing tokens and explain how Raft keeps a log consistent.
days.deliverable: Leader election demo and Raft notes
checks: Only one worker acts as leader
Fencing tokens stop the old leader's writes
Log replication explained with a diagram

subtopics: Events as the backbone of systems
days.lab_task: Design a real-time fraud detection system on an event stream with windows and joins, show how replay rebuilds state and explain delivery guarantees.
checks: Window and join choices match the fraud rules

days.topic: API Design for Large Systems: REST, gRPC and GraphQL Choices
days.lab_task: Choose API styles for public, mobile and internal parts of a marketplace, design a long-running export operation and define pagination and versioning rules.
checks: Each API style justified by its clients
Export uses a job resource with status polling

days.topic: Reliability: Redundancy, Failover and Disaster Recovery
subtopics: Availability numbers and what they mean
days.lab_task: Raise a single-region design to 99.99 percent availability with redundancy, failover and multi-zone deployment, set RPO and RTO and choose a disaster recovery strategy.
checks: RPO and RTO chosen per data store

days.topic: Observability Design: Metrics, Logs and Traces
subtopics: What to measure in a system
days.lab_task: Add an observability design to the chat system with golden signals, SLOs, tracing across gateways and storage, alerts and dashboards for on-call engineers and managers.
checks: SLOs set for sending and delivering messages
Trace spans cover the message path

subtopics: Data protection at rest and in transit
days.lab_task: Threat model the payment system with STRIDE, add authentication, authorisation, encryption, secrets management, abuse protection and audit logging, and update the design.
checks: Each high threat has a control
Sensitive actions recorded in an audit log

days.topic: Low-Level Design: Concurrency and Thread Safety
subtopics: Deadlocks and how to avoid them
days.lab_task: Fix race conditions in a ticket booking module, build a producer-consumer pipeline, create and then fix a deadlock and write tests that catch concurrency bugs.
checks: No double-booked seats under concurrent load

days.topic: Low-Level Design Problems: Elevator, Splitwise and BookMyShow
subtopics: Seat booking with locking and timeouts
days.lab_task: Design and code an elevator controller, an expense-splitting app and a movie seat booking system with class diagrams, patterns, concurrency handling and tests.
days.deliverable: Three low-level designs with code and tests
checks: Controller serves requests in a sensible order
Expense app settles debts with the fewest payments
Seat holds expire and never double-book

days.topic: Interview Practice: Mock High-Level and Low-Level Design Sessions
subtopics: Interview formats at product and service companies
Time plans for 45 and 60 minute rounds
days.lab_task: Run two timed mock interviews, one high-level and one low-level, with peers scoring against a rubric, then write a revision plan for the weakest areas.
checks: Design completed within the time limit

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Designing a Food Delivery Platform
days.lab_task: Design a food delivery platform with ordering, restaurant and rider matching, live tracking, payments, notifications, reliability and observability, code the order allocation module and defend the design.
days.deliverable: Design document, code and defence recording
checks: Panel questions on scale and failure answered
Allocation code handles concurrency and tests pass
objectives: Combine the intermediate topics in one design

advanced.summary: For senior and staff engineers and architects. Covers large-scale case studies, global multi-region systems, geo-distributed databases and consistency models, and designs for a distributed message queue, distributed cache, object storage, metrics platform, job scheduler, search engine, recommendation system, ad click aggregation, stock exchange and LLM application platform, plus capacity and cost modelling, batch and stream architectures, reliability at scale, decision records, design reviews and staff-level interviews.
prerequisites: Solid experience with intermediate system design topics
Has designed or owned production systems
outcomes: Model capacity, cost and reliability with numbers
Perform at senior and staff-level design interviews

subtopics: Evolution of large architectures over time
Applying lessons to your own systems
days.lab_task: Analyse three published architecture evolutions and two outage post-mortems, extract recurring patterns and anti-patterns and apply them to a design you own.
days.deliverable: Case study analysis and applied lessons
checks: Key decisions and their reasons extracted
Design lessons drawn from each post-mortem
Own design updated with two lessons

days.lab_task: Design a global collaboration product with users in India, Europe and the US, data residency rules, active-active regions, conflict handling and failover targets.
days.deliverable: Global design with latency and cost analysis
checks: User data stays in the required regions
Conflict resolution defined for concurrent edits
Cost of the multi-region design estimated

tools: Case studies of Spanner, CockroachDB and DynamoDB global tables
days.lab_task: Compare three geo-distributed databases for a banking ledger and a shopping cart, show anomalies under weaker isolation and design a CRDT-based cart.
checks: Write skew example demonstrated under snapshot isolation
Cart merges concurrent edits without conflicts

subtopics: Replication and leader election per partition
days.lab_task: Design a Kafka-like distributed queue from scratch with partitioned logs, replication, consumer groups and delivery guarantees, and estimate broker capacity.
checks: Partition leaders and followers handle broker loss
Brokers needed for the target throughput estimated

subtopics: Consistency with the source of truth
days.lab_task: Design a distributed cache service for many teams with partitioning, replication, eviction, hot key protection and consistency rules, and estimate memory and node counts.
checks: Hot key traffic spread or coalesced
Invalidation rules keep data within the freshness target

days.lab_task: Design an S3-like object store with separate metadata and data paths, erasure coding, placement across failure domains, multipart uploads and storage tiers, and calculate durability.
days.deliverable: Object storage design with durability calculation
checks: Design reaches eleven nines with stated assumptions
Large uploads resumable and assembled correctly

days.topic: Designing a Metrics and Monitoring System
days.lab_task: Design a monitoring platform that ingests ten million samples per second, stores and downsamples series, handles high cardinality and evaluates alerts for many tenants.
checks: Ingestion path handles the target rate
Limits and storage design for high cardinality

subtopics: Requirements: delayed, recurring and dependent jobs
tools: Scheduler references such as Airflow and Temporal
days.lab_task: Design a scheduler for one billion jobs a day with delayed and recurring jobs, leases, retries, fairness between tenants and dependency workflows.
checks: Crashed workers' jobs picked up after lease expiry

days.lab_task: Design a web-scale search engine with an indexing pipeline, sharded inverted indexes, query fan-out, ranking and freshness, and estimate index size and query capacity.
checks: Inverted index sharding and replication described
New pages searchable within the target time
Index size and query capacity estimated

days.lab_task: Design recommendations for a video app with candidate generation, ranking, a feature store, real-time signals, cold-start handling and A/B evaluation.
checks: Candidate generation and ranking stages defined
New users and items get sensible recommendations

days.topic: Designing an Ad Click Aggregation System
days.lab_task: Design click aggregation for billions of events a day with windowed counts, late event handling, deduplication, batch reconciliation and fast dashboard queries.
checks: Late clicks counted in the right window

days.lab_task: Design an exchange with a deterministic matching engine, sequenced inputs, market data fan-out, risk checks and failover, and code a price-time priority order book.
days.deliverable: Exchange design and order book code
checks: Order book matches by price then time
Standby continues with no lost orders

subtopics: Requirements for AI features at scale
days.lab_task: Design a platform that serves AI assistants for many product teams with a model gateway, retrieval, caching, guardrails, quotas, evaluation and cost tracking.
checks: Requests routed by cost, latency and capability
Quotas and caching keep cost within budget

days.lab_task: Build a capacity and cost model for the video platform for three years, test it against growth scenarios and present cost-aware design changes.
checks: Capacity per component calculated for each year
Model updated for high and low growth
Two design changes reduce cost with impact stated

days.topic: Data-Intensive Design: Batch, Stream and Lambda or Kappa Architectures
days.lab_task: Design analytics for a ride-sharing company with lambda and kappa variants, compare correctness, cost and complexity, and choose one.
checks: Batch and speed layers merge correctly
Choice justified by cost and correctness

days.lab_task: Redesign a large service for reliability with cells, admission control and retry budgets, explain a metastable failure and design a chaos programme to find weaknesses.
checks: Failure in one cell limited to its users
Retry budgets and backoff stop amplification

days.topic: Architecture Decision Records and Trade-off Analysis
subtopics: Building a decision log for a team
days.lab_task: Write decision records for five choices in the food delivery design with trade-off matrices, mark which are reversible and define fitness functions that check two of them.
checks: Each record has context, options and consequences

days.topic: Reviewing Designs and Leading Design Discussions
subtopics: Bringing in security, reliability and cost views
days.lab_task: Lead a design review of a classmate's design with a checklist, facilitate a disagreement to a decision, write outcomes and actions and follow up on one action.
checks: At least five real risks found
Disagreement resolved with a recorded decision

subtopics: What changes at senior and staff level
days.lab_task: Complete two staff-level mock interviews on open-ended problems, review recordings against a senior rubric and write a practice plan for the next month.
days.deliverable: Mock interview recordings, scores and practice plan
checks: Deep-dive answered with numbers and trade-offs

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Designing a Global Event Ticketing Platform
days.lab_task: Design a global ticketing platform that survives on-sale traffic spikes with fair queuing, seat inventory consistency, payments, fraud checks, multi-region reliability and cost modelling, then defend it to a review panel.
days.deliverable: Design document, models, decision log and defence recording
checks: Design handles the stated peak with fair queuing
No seat sold twice in any failure case
Review panel questions answered with evidence
objectives: Combine the advanced topics in one design
